name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.existsUnique_affineExtension_closedBall
title: Affine extension from equal-radius closed balls

content.display_title: Affine extension from equal-radius closed balls
content.one_sentence_role: Recovers the centers, matches the interiors, and then extends across the boundary.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces, $c\in E$, $d\in F$, and $r>0$. Write $\overline B(c,r)=\{x:\|x-c\|\le r\}$. Every bijective isometry $f:\overline B(c,r)\to\overline B(d,r)$ extends uniquely to a surjective real affine isometry $A:E\to F$. The extension satisfies $A(x)=f(x)$ for every point of the source closed ball.
content.assumptions: The source and target closed balls have the same positive radius $r$. No completeness or finite dimensionality is assumed.
content.conclusion: There is one and only one ambient affine isometry agreeing with the given $f$ on the entire closed ball, including its boundary.
content.proof_summary: Use bounded reflection symmetry to send the centers to each other. The resulting distance-to-center identity verifies the interior equivalence required by the convex extension theorem.
proof_steps: The centers belong to their balls since $r>0$, and the source ball is bounded. Reflection through $c$ preserves its ball because $\|(2c-x)-c\|=\|x-c\|$, and similarly for $d$; see [Center reflection preserves a closed ball](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Ball.lean#L35-L39). Apply [Center transport by point reflection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/Reflection.lean#L74-L91) to these two balls and their centers to obtain $f(c)=d$.

For every $x\in\overline B(c,r)$, $$\|f(x)-d\|=\|f(x)-f(c)\|=\|x-c\|.$$ For a positive radius, the ambient interior of each closed ball is its corresponding open ball. Therefore $$\begin{aligned}x\in\operatorname{int}\overline B(c,r)&\Longleftrightarrow\|x-c\|<r\\&\Longleftrightarrow\|f(x)-d\|<r\\&\Longleftrightarrow f(x)\in\operatorname{int}\overline B(d,r).\end{aligned}$$ The common radius is used in the middle equivalence.

The source closed ball is convex and its interior contains $c$. These facts and Step 2 verify [Extension through a dense convex interior](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Convex.lean#L51-L95) for the same $f$. That theorem returns the unique ambient extension with agreement on the whole source set, so it includes the boundary points as well.
